observations:
Torah #105 has only 2 bechina edges in the dataset, forming a single 3-node connected component (Package 1). The threshold for a new package proposal is 3+ concepts sharing a bechina domain that is independent and not covered by the existing package structure.

Two gap concepts were identified in the source text (זמרת יה and גלות השכינה — see torah_105_additions.json), but neither constitutes an independent new package:

1. זִמְרַת יָהּ — This concept naturally extends Package 1 (Simple Mercy / God's Prayer) as a scriptural name for תפלת הקדוש ברוך הוא. It is a one-node addition to an existing package, not a new domain.

2. גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה — This represents the negative/evil pole of the Torah's teaching. However, it appears as a single bechina statement ('וְזֶה בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה') without additional bechina-linked companions that would form a cluster. The evil condition is described narratively in eitza terms (sin → letters expelled → da'at disturbed → exile of Shekhinah) not through multiple bechina equivalences.

The Torah's conceptual structure is deliberately streamlined: the Rebbe presents a single, focused argument moving from Torah study through a chain of cause-and-effect to complete redemption. The bechina layer captures only the essential identity at the heart of that argument — the equivalence of simple mercy, Zeir Anpin's mercy, and God's own prayer. Everything else is eitza.

Candidates examined and rejected:
- Torah / עז / תשובה: These three concepts interact heavily in the Torah but always through eitza relationships (Torah LEADS TO Teshuva, Torah ENABLES God's prayer). There are zero bechina edges connecting them to each other within Torah #105. They do not form a bechina package.
- da'at / rachamut / teshuva: Same analysis — these are causal-chain concepts (eitza) within this Torah, not co-essential bechina equivalences. The famous bechina of da'at = rachamut appears in other Torahs but is not expressed as a bechina edge in Torah #105.

Conclusion: The single Package 1 (רַחֲמִים פְּשׁוּטִים וּתְפִלַּת הַשֵּׁם) fully accounts for all bechina-connected nodes in the Torah #105 dataset. No new package is warranted.
